wheat.name: Nitrogen Deficiency (Chlorosis)
evidence: Uniform yellowing beginning at the tips of older lower leaves (V-shaped pattern)
No fungal spore pustules or powdery dusting on white cloth rub test
Overall stunted tillering and pale light green canopy appearance
recommendedActions: Foliar spray 2% Urea solution (20g Urea per 1 litre of clean water) during late afternoon hours
Top-dress 30-35 kg/acre Urea after immediate light irrigation once soil moisture permits walking
Incorporate well-rotted vermicompost (5 quintals/acre) in subsequent Rabi preparation
preventivePractices: Split nitrogen into 3 doses: 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at CRI stage (21 days), and 1/3 at tillering (42 days)
Conduct pre-sowing soil test for available nitrogen

wheat.name: Stripe Rust / Yellow Rust
evidence: Linear yellow-orange powdery pustules formed along leaf veins
Bright yellow urediniospores rub off easily onto fingers or white cotton cloth
Favored by persistent morning dew, cloudiness, and cool daytime temperatures (10-20°C)
recommendedActions: Immediately isolate affected patches and avoid walking from diseased to healthy fields
Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 200 ml OR Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 200 ml in 200 L water per acre
Repeat spray after 12-15 days only if weather remains overcast and new active stripes emerge
preventivePractices: Cultivate resistant wheat varieties recommended for NWPZ (e.g. DBW-187, DBW-303, HD-3226)
Avoid late sowing beyond November 25 in sub-mountainous tracts of Punjab and Haryana

wheat.name: Loose Smut of Wheat
evidence: Entire earhead transformed into black powdery spore mass replacing healthy grains
Silvery membrane surrounding the smutted spike bursts upon ear emergence
recommendedActions: Carefully rogue out diseased ears in polythene bags to prevent wind dispersal and bury deep
Do not use seed from this harvest for next season's crop
preventivePractices: Mandatory pre-sowing seed treatment with Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% (Vitavax Power) @ 2.5 g/kg seed
Use certified breeder/foundation seed from National Seeds Corporation
warningSigns: Wind-borne spread to adjacent flowering wheat spikes

mustard.name: Alternaria Leaf Blight
evidence: Circular to oval brown necrotic lesions on leaves with characteristic concentric rings
Lesions coalesce causing leaf blight, defoliation, and stem spotting during foggy weather
recommendedActions: Foliar spray Mancozeb 75% WP (Indofil M-45) @ 500-600 g in 200 litres water per acre
Apply 10% boiled neem leaf extract as an organic bio-fungicide during early vegetative stage
preventivePractices: Seed treatment with Apron 35 SD @ 6 g/kg or Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/kg seed
Maintain adequate crop spacing (30 x 10 cm) to ensure good aeration
warningSigns: Pod infection causing premature shrivelled seeds

mustard.name: White Rust / Blister
evidence: Prominent white or creamy chalk-like raised blisters on leaf undersides
Floral malformation resulting in swollen, sterile 'staghead' spikes
recommendedActions: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% (Ridomil MZ) @ 500 g per 200 litres water per acre
Remove and destroy malformed staghead floral spikes
preventivePractices: Sow early in October before temperatures dip below 18°C

paddy.name: Yellow Stem Borer
evidence: Central shoot withers and dries up causing 'Dead Heart' in tillering stage
Panicle turns completely white and grainless ('White Earhead') during reproductive stage
Small entry holes plugged with excreta visible near base of the stem
recommendedActions: Broadcast Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR (Ferterra) @ 4 kg/acre mixed with dry sand
Install 4-5 sex pheromone traps per acre for pest monitoring
preventivePractices: Clip seedling leaf tips before nursery transplanting to remove egg masses
Avoid excessive nitrogen application which makes succulent stems prone to attack
warningSigns: More than 5% dead hearts or 1 moth per square metre
